name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,252

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pancake with ham’s filling at parties

indicators.note: a filling sits inside, so only the central letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: dos (do's) are parties or celebrations
the middle letter of ham

explanation.surface: Someone serves pancakes stuffed with ham at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at parties' places the kept letter after DOS. A dosa is a South Indian rice-and-lentil pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosa is a thin fermented crêpe from southern India, a kind of savoury flat griddle cake.

clue.text: Before chasing shot, racket is just the thing?

indicators.note: before tells us which piece is written first in the line of letters
something shot is ruined or broken up, so the letters of the neighbouring word are scrambled

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise, a racket
the letters of chasing, rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of a drink after a stiff shot, with noise being exactly what's needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing shot' reads like a chaser after a drink, but chasing is the fodder and shot rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kant's German phrase means the thing in itself, reality independent of perception; 'just the thing' is a playful gloss on that.

clue.text: Elaborate, that hoax, escorting demos

indicators.note: the escorting word carries letters across the join, and in a reverse clue they are to be read in the upward direction

blocks.note: the end of hoax and the start of escorting run together as three letters
demos means demonstrates: in this reverse clue the fragment shows a word going upwards, so the direction becomes part of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to embellish the hoax, accompanying some demonstration recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse cryptic: the answer read as an instruction, a short word going up, describes what happens across 'hoax, escorting', and 'demos' says the clue shows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex up a story is to make it more exciting by embellishing or exaggerating, which is elaborating it.

clue.text: Crosspiece not attached, except when bearing weight

indicators.note: something bearing a load carries it within, so the first word holds the abbreviation inside

blocks.note: single means unmarried, not attached to a partner
W is the abbreviation for weight
bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A rule about a crosspiece: it stays free unless it carries a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not attached' looks like a description of the crosspiece but means unmarried, and 'except' is the preposition bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A swingle-bar is the pivoted crossbar on a carriage to which the traces of a harnessed horse are fastened.

clue.text: Lightness of touch of lord, leading royal to break rank

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the lord's abbreviation comes ahead of the royal
breaking into something means getting inside it, so this pair is placed within the word for rank

blocks.note: L is an abbreviation for lord
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher
rank as in foul-smelling, whiffy

explanation.surface: A lord ahead of a royal breaks out of line, done with a light touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' suggests a row or a title, but here it means smelly. ER is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Whifflery is trifling levity, frivolous behaviour; a light, flippant touch is the sense the clue reaches for.

clue.text: Finishes off an Inveraray tea of loaf and local trifle?

indicators.note: the finishes of words are their end letters, so the last letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: the final letters of an, Inveraray, tea, of, loaf

explanation.surface: Someone polishes off a Highland tea of bread and a Scottish trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: Inveraray is a town in Argyll, which hints at the Scots word; 'local' means dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a nyaff is a small, worthless or insignificant person, a mere nobody or trifle of a man.

clue.text: Small stones thrown out round island houses I’m going to

indicators.note: a house holds its occupants, so the first pair of pieces wraps around the contraction that follows

blocks.note: a lap is one round of a track
I is an abbreviation for island
I'll, the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Pebbles flung round an island's houses that someone means to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: LAP and I together hold I'LL: LAP + ILL + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapilli are small fragments of lava ejected by a volcano during an eruption, hence stones thrown out.

clue.text: Behind front of market, stacks one’s fish

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a bum is a behind, the backside
first letter of market
stacks means a lot, a great amount
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Behind the front of a market stall, someone piles up fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition but is the noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The bummalo or bummaloti is a small South Asian fish, dried and sold as Bombay duck.

clue.text: Cold deserts rugged, misty in places

indicators.note: deserting means abandoning, so the abbreviation walks out of the word

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rugged, rocky ground

explanation.surface: A cold, rugged landscape, foggy here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in places' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roky is a regional word for foggy or smoky, used in some dialects of English for hazy weather.

clue.text: Men rising to boot around large weight

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned round
around means surrounding, so the phrase for 'as well' wraps the abbreviation

blocks.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
to boot means as well, too
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand up to kick something round a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' looks like kicking but means 'as well'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotolo is an old Italian unit of mass, the Italian form of the rotl, a pound used in Mediterranean trade.

clue.text: IOC man stumbling across university rugby team’s drug

indicators.note: someone stumbling has lost their footing, so these letters fall into a new order
lying across something means spanning it, so the rearranged letters sit either side of the rest

blocks.note: taken as written; IOC is the International Olympic Committee
U is the abbreviation for university
a rugby union side has fifteen players, XV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An Olympic official trips while crossing to a university rugby team's drug supply, a doping story.
explanation.definitionFit: Nux vomica is the seed of an Asian tree yielding strychnine, used in medicine and homeopathy.

clue.text: Ruse Muslim maybe got from naval officer — short type

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the word for type loses its final letter

blocks.note: PO, petty officer in the navy
a type or brand, a make

explanation.surface: A trick involving a Muslim, extracted from a naval officer of a brief type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruse' is not a trick but Ruse, a city in Bulgaria, home to Muslim Bulgarians.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomaks are Bulgarian-speaking Muslims of the Balkans, so a Muslim from Ruse could well be one.

clue.text: No longer sanction putting upper limit on software

indicators.note: an upper limit is a ceiling placed after the first word, as a cap is placed over something

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software
a roof is a ceiling, an upper limit

explanation.surface: Withdrawing approval for a program by capping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Approof is an archaic noun for approval or sanction, now obsolete in English usage.

clue.text: Die half numb, after stripping for a ramble

indicators.note: stripping removes the outer covering, so only the inner letters remain
letters going for a ramble wander off and return in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
numb without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone half frozen, having undressed, nearly dies on a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' looks like a verb but is the noun, a dice. Fulham is also a London district, here irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: In old gaming slang a fulham was a loaded die, weighted to cheat at dice games.

clue.text: Drug that’s rather popular gone into by chap with tablet

indicators.note: being gone into means having something enter you, so the word for chap is set inside
with means accompanied by, so the tablet's letter is added at the end

blocks.note: a tad means slightly, rather
a chap is a man
in means fashionable, popular
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A fashionable drug that a man swallows along with a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather popular' is one unit, a tad in, which the man enters after its opening letter. E is slang for an ecstasy pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Amantadine is an antiviral medicine also prescribed to treat the symptoms of Parkinson's disease.

clue.text: Look to be in range, meaning mostly to remain within what’s expected of centipedes

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the interjection goes within the word for range
mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
remaining within means staying enclosed, so the shortened word sits inside the next

blocks.note: scope is range or extent
lo, an old word meaning look
the norm is what is expected or standard
the drift of an argument is its meaning

explanation.surface: Instructions to look within range and keep meaning within what is expected, ending abruptly with centipedes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs as two containers in a row; 'of centipedes' is the definition, an adjective phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Scolopendra is a genus of large centipedes, so scolopendriform describes something shaped like those creatures.

clue.text: Craven, maybe, after turning up to counter Native Americans

indicators.note: turning up in a down answer means flipping to read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a chip is a counter used in gambling
Wes Craven was an American horror film director

explanation.surface: A coward, perhaps, after showing up to oppose American tribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craven' reads as cowardly but is the surname of the American horror director Wes Craven.
explanation.definitionFit: Otchipwe is a variant name for the Ojibwa, an Algonquian people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Welshman having pound bet giving away tips and drinks

indicators.note: having means holding alongside, so the Welshman is followed by the rest
giving away the tips means losing the end letters of each word

blocks.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name
a quid is a pound sterling
a risk is a gamble, a bet

explanation.surface: A Welshman with a pound wager won't tip the bar staff and buys cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: Both QUID and RISK lose their final letters. Dai is the stock Welshman of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Daiquiris are cocktails of rum, lime juice and sugar, named after a Cuban town.

clue.text: Making typically London company with City finance ok, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together in an unspecified order

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company passes City of London money as fine, giving it a London character.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; a Cockney is a working-class East Londoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneyfication is the process of turning something into the speech or style of a Cockney Londoner.

clue.text: Alliance crossing border once, never again

indicators.note: the alliance's name crosses over the border word, enclosing it from either side

blocks.note: NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization alliance
a hem is a border or edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A military alliance once crossed a frontier and vows never to repeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word, here a Spenserian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathemo is an old Spenserian adverb meaning never the more, no more, so never again.

clue.text: Fern in area covering the whole of Australia, from the south

indicators.note: in a down answer covering means sitting on top, so the area letter comes first
read from the south of a down answer, the letters run from bottom to top

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
the whole means all
Oz is a nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A fern growing in a region spreads over all of Australia, starting in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Azolla is a genus of tiny floating water ferns, found in ponds and paddy fields worldwide.

clue.text: Joint which lies to the west, out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds are the outermost letters, and being out of them leaves just the inner ones
going west in an across answer means travelling right to left

blocks.note: which is that and lies are fibs; the joined pair loses its two outermost letters

explanation.surface: A hip joint, which lies westward, off limits to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: THATFIBS loses its first and last letters, and HATFIB is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Biftah is slang for a cannabis cigarette, a joint in the drug-taking sense rather than a body part.

clue.text: One pursuing golf with time going for latest in clubs getting hole in one

indicators.note: the latest in a sequence is the last, so the final letter of the word is kept
one thing going for another means making way for it, a swap of letters

blocks.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet Hotel comes straight after Golf
T is the abbreviation for time
the last letter of clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer with time to spare gets the latest clubs and hits a hole in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' is a word of the phonetic alphabet, not the game, and S replaces the T in HOTEL. The definition is cryptic: the hole sits in one club.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosel is the socket in a golf club's head into which the shaft fits, a hole in the club itself.

clue.text: Use fleas, oddly, after receiving staff’s order for newts

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd positions only
receiving means taking something in, so the staff goes inside the selected letters

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of use fleas
a rod is a staff

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to put fleas to use once a staff has been handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Urodela is the zoological order of tailed amphibians, comprising newts and salamanders.

clue.text: Object to Scot removing header from form

indicators.note: the header is the top letter of a down answer, and removing it drops the first letter

blocks.note: a form is a bench, as is a settle

explanation.surface: A Scotsman protests at being taken off the header of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest but is the noun aim, and 'form' is a bench, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots ettle means an aim or intention, so an object or purpose to a Scotsman.

clue.text: Say that pub must shut in blow to Dundonians

indicators.note: shutting something in encloses it, so the abbreviation for say is held inside

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A demand that a Dundee pub be closed, a blow to the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a Scottish city, so 'Dundonians' marks a Scots word; 'blow' means pant, not a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegh is a Scots verb meaning to pant or puff for breath, which is to blow.

clue.text: Case coming from pocket found on alien

indicators.note: found on means placed beside, so the second piece follows the alien's letters

blocks.note: ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film
pocket as an adjective means small, wee

explanation.surface: A case pulled out of the pocket of an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocket' looks like a noun but serves as the adjective small, as in pocket-sized.
explanation.definitionFit: Etwee is an old spelling of etui, a small ornamental case for needles or toiletries.

clue.text: Guards in thoroughfare on left I spot cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter of the word moves to the front

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
re means about, on
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a zit is a spot or pimple

explanation.surface: Sentries posted on a road see someone spot a cyclist on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the preposition re, meaning about. The strelitzi were Russian, so the plural ends in I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Streltsy, or strelitzi, were Russian guards, an elite musketeer corps of the tsars disbanded by Peter the Great.

clue.text: A chap’s personal explosive is presumably … for opening cell?

blocks.clueFragment: A chap’s personal explosive is presumably … for opening cell?
blocks.note: surface reading: a safe-breaker's charge, which is his own to set off to open a prison cell

blocks.clueFragment: A chap’s personal explosive is presumably …
blocks.note: setter's reading: the gap is filled by the answer split into three words meaning it belongs to him to detonate

explanation.surface: A prisoner's own explosive charge is surely his to set off to break out of his cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap with HIS TO BLAST and the sentence reads naturally; then the whole word means a biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A histoblast is a cell that gives rise to tissue in a developing organism, a formative tissue cell.

clue.text: Pair caught napping, each losing diamonds one plucked from Africa

indicators.note: each losing means every one of the pair gives something up, so the card-suit abbreviation is dropped twice

blocks.note: a sleeper's snore is written zz, two zeds
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Two card players caught dozing each lose their diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one plucked' is not something taken away but an instrument whose strings are plucked.
explanation.definitionFit: The zeze is a stringed folk instrument of East Africa, a fiddle or zither played by plucking.
